merges.why: Each treatment is one block of a single long treatments page with a jump board at the top, instead of a dozen thin pages.
Every kind of booking belongs on one Book online page; the emergency slot is also a section here and the Emergency page links to it.
Fees, membership, insurance and finance all answer the question of what it costs and how to pay.
Forms are part of preparing for a first visit.
Technology and clinic tour support the practice story and standards.
Parents look for children and family care together, and both serve the same audience.
Home-care guides and aftercare instructions are both practical patient advice.

merged.why: Only two sections (pain and comfort, safety and X-rays). Cost, cancellations and emergencies are promised but not shown, and those topics are already covered on Prices, Book online and Emergency dentist.

remaining: repeated: Sedation and numbing options for nervous patients
repeated: Hygiene, sterilisation and infection control standards

homeSectionIdeas: Hero with a welcoming photo, 'Book an appointment' button and emergency phone number
Quick-access tiles: check-up, emergency, whitening, aligners, children
Meet your dentists strip with friendly portraits
How your first visit works in three steps
Opening hours, location map and new-patient welcome offer
styleNotes: Clean, bright layout with lots of white space that feels hygienic and calm.
Soft blues, teals or fresh greens with one warm accent for buttons, avoiding clinical harshness.
Real, smiling photos of the team and clinic rather than stock imagery, with rounded shapes to feel gentle.
Large readable type and sticky phone and booking buttons so anxious or urgent visitors act easily on mobile.
